subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: Das and Naglieri's cognitive-processing theory of intelligence describes four interconnected components — Planning, Attention, and two forms of information processing (Simultaneous and Successive). This model, based on neuropsychological functioning rather than a single IQ score, is known as the:
explanation: The PASS Model (Planning, Attention, Simultaneous, Successive processing), proposed by J.P. Das and Jack Naglieri, is grounded in Luria's neuropsychological work on brain functioning — distinct from Sternberg's Triarchic Theory (analytical/practical/creative) or Guilford's Structure of Intellect (a psychometric factor model).
